chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-A'la, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (peace be upon them both) who said:
When you enter a thicket and find eggs, do not eat from them except what differs in its two ends (i.e., oblong-shaped eggs).

key_terms.أَجَمَة: A dense thicket, woodland, or bush — a wild environment where game birds nest
key_terms.طَرَفَاهُ: Its two ends/extremities — refers to the two poles of the egg; 'different' means one end is more pointed than the other (oblong shape)

ai.seo_question: How do you identify which wild eggs are permissible to eat according to Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from one of the two Imams (al-Baqir or al-Sadiq, peace be upon them) establishes a practical jurisprudential rule for identifying permissible wild eggs. The ruling instructs that eggs found in the wild should only be consumed if they are oblong (with one end distinctly different from the other), as this shape is characteristic of birds with gizzards (a sign of permissibility), unlike round eggs which may belong to forbidden reptiles or birds. This distinction reflects the Imams' guidance on applying fiqh principles to everyday foraging situations.
word_analysis: one of the two of them
